description: One step of a period close: what has to be done, whether it is required before the period may be locked, and — once somebody has done it — who and when. The Spanish label is beside the English rather than in a translation file because the person ticking 'conciliación bancaria hecha' on a phone in a packing shed is reading this row, not a PO file somebody has to remember to regenerate.

fields.description: What has to happen, in the imperative — 'Reconcile every bank account', 'Post accruals', 'Run depreciation'.
fields.label: Step

fields.description: The same step in Spanish. Optional: a step with no Spanish is shown in English rather than hidden, because a missing translation must never make a required close step invisible to the person who has to do it.
fields.label: Step (Español)

fields.description: The order a closer works in. Display and sort only — nothing enforces that step 3 waits for step 2, because a real close runs several steps in parallel and a system that pretended otherwise would be worked around on the first busy month.
fields.label: Sequence

fields.description: Whether the `closing_checklist` control counts this step when the period is closed. UNTICKED IS A REAL AND USEFUL ANSWER: a step somebody wants tracked but not gated — 'email the lender the flash figures' — belongs on the list without being able to hold the close.
fields.label: Required To Close

fields.description: Set by complete_checklist_item, together with who and when. Tick it by hand in the Desk and the same thing happens; the attribution comes off the session either way.
fields.label: Done

fields.description: What backs the tick — a reconciliation docname, a report reference, a journal entry. A checklist of bare ticks is a claim; a checklist of ticks that each point at something is evidence, and this column is the whole of that difference.
fields.label: Evidence

name: Closing Checklist Item
